words.sense: make an action or outcome impossible in advance
misconceptions: Not being selected for a group is always prevention of an event

words.sense: leave someone or something outside a defined group
misconceptions: An obstacle preventing an event always removes someone from membership

semantic_axes.description: Blocking an outcome before it can happen differs from leaving a person or item outside a group.

edges.boundary_rule: preclude makes an event impossible; exclude leaves someone or something out of a group.
clues_a: rule blocks an event from happening
clues_b: one item left out of selection

misconceptions.M1: Assumes every prevention is group exclusion
misconceptions.M2: Assumes removing an item from a set is preventing an event
misconceptions.M3: Confuses a rejected invitation with an impossible event

chains.frame: Which word best describes what the exam schedule did to Zahra’s trip?

beats.text: Zahra’s final exam was fixed for the exact time of the trip, so she could not go.
beats.decisive_clue: clashing schedules made the trip impossible
beats.reason: The issue is preventing the planned activity.

beats.text: She had already packed her bag the evening before.
beats.reason: Packing does not alter the scheduling barrier.

chains.feedback_short: Key evidence: timing still made attendance impossible.
chains.feedback_deep: preclude means to prevent a possibility or event from occurring; exclude means to omit or keep someone or something out of a group. The issue is preventing the planned activity. Packing does not alter the scheduling barrier.
chains.contrast_rule: preclude makes an event impossible; exclude leaves someone or something out of a group.

hints.axis: Blocking an outcome before it can happen differs from leaving a person or item outside a group.
hints.contrast: preclude makes an event impossible; exclude leaves someone or something out of a group.

beats.text: The coordinator deliberately left Theo off the volunteer list while including the other applicants.

beats.reason: This is non-inclusion in a roster.

beats.text: The list was printed on yellow paper.
beats.decisive_clue: name still omitted from the roster
beats.reason: Paper colour does not change membership.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what the storm did to Amara’s family visit?

beats.text: Flooded roads made it impossible for Amara to reach her family’s gathering that weekend.
beats.reason: The roads blocked an event from taking place.

beats.text: Even the alternate road was underwater, leaving no workable route.
beats.decisive_clue: no possible route to the planned visit

chains.feedback_short: New confirmation: no possible route to the planned visit.
chains.feedback_deep: preclude means to prevent a possibility or event from occurring; exclude means to omit or keep someone or something out of a group. The roads blocked an event from taking place. The extra information confirms prevention.
chains.contrast_rule: preclude makes an event impossible; exclude leaves someone or something out of a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes how Mateo handled one photograph?

beats.text: Mateo left a blurry photograph out of the ten pictures selected for the family album.
beats.decisive_clue: item removed from a selected set
beats.reason: The issue is omission from a collection.

beats.text: He selected nine sharp photographs but not the blurry one.
beats.decisive_clue: photograph not included in chosen set
beats.reason: The count confirms which item was left out.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what the passport delay did to Nika’s departure?

beats.text: Nika’s passport was not ready before the flight, making the journey impossible on that date.
beats.reason: The obstacle blocks the event before it can happen.

beats.text: The airline never removed her from its passenger list; she simply could not travel without the document.
beats.decisive_clue: departure blocked without being removed from a group
beats.reason: The booking status clarifies that the problem is impossibility, not omission from the passenger list.

chains.feedback_short: The clarification points to: departure blocked without being removed from a group.
chains.feedback_deep: preclude means to prevent a possibility or event from occurring; exclude means to omit or keep someone or something out of a group. The obstacle blocks the event before it can happen. The booking status clarifies that the problem is impossibility, not omission from the passenger list.
chains.contrast_rule: preclude makes an event impossible; exclude leaves someone or something out of a group.

hints.attention: Distinguish the booking from the ability to board.
